title: An r-partite ordered hypergraph matching realising prescribed clique-size bounds via a monotone point set

core_obligations: Parameterise the patterns: every pattern of the finest ordered partition of r corresponds to a unique function tau with tau(1) = 1, so the prescribed bounds can be indexed by those functions (proof lines 564-565).

Apply the multi-dimensional Erdos-Szekeres theorem: the author's theorem gives a point collection Z in R^r of the required size whose coordinates are all distinct and whose tau-monotone sequences have the prescribed bounded lengths (proof lines 565).

Build the matching from the point set: the intervals determined by the coordinates of each point give the r edges of the corresponding edge of the matching, and the distinctness of the coordinates makes the edges pairwise disjoint (proof lines 566-571).

Verify the clique-size bounds: a P-clique of the matching corresponds to a monotone sequence in Z, so the bound on monotone sequences transfers to L_P, while for all other patterns the automatic bound L_P = 1 holds (proof lines 570-571).
proof_roadmap: 把最细划分的 pattern 用函数 tau 参数化，并把给定的 m_P 记作 m_tau。
用多维 Erdős–Szekeres 定理取得坐标互异、各 tau-单调子列长度不超过 m_tau 的点集 Z；由每个点的坐标区间造出一条边，得到 r-partite 匹配；单调子列与 P-团的对应把界转移过来。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the construction lemma that turns a monotone point set into an ordered hypergraph matching with prescribed clique-size bounds (author lemma at source lines 556-560, label obs-construction-partite). The proof (source lines 564-571) is the author's own, headed Proof of Lemma obs-construction-partite, and it is a clean correspondence argument: the patterns of the finest partition are parameterised by the monotone functions tau, the author's multi-dimensional Erdos-Szekeres theorem provides a point set with distinct coordinates whose tau-monotone sequences are bounded by the prescribed integers, and the coordinates of each point produce the edges of the matching, so that a P-clique corresponds precisely to a monotone sequence and the bounds transfer (proof lines 565-571). The lemma is the building block that the paper's lower-bound theorem iterates. H2.
